$comment: Ingredient synonym table. scripts/build.mjs tries three ways to turn a node's `inputs` into a real `from` link: (1) the string is already a node id, (2) it normalises to a node name, (3) it matches a key here. This file is case 3 -- the explicit, reviewable part. Keys are matched against a lowercased, punctuation-stripped form of the input string. Values are node ids in this tree.
$note: Tungsten, cobalt and the rare earths each have a canonical metal node now (`metal.tungsten`, `metal.cobalt`, `metal.rare-earths`), so the tungsten, cobalt and bastnasite strings above point at the substance rather than at the nearest thing that happened to mention it. "tungsten ore" points at the ore node and "tungsten wire" at the wire: build.mjs matches a key only when the string does not already resolve by id or by unique name, so the split is deliberate. Two cobalt keys deserve care. "cobalt" and "cobalt metal" point at the metal, which is what a carbide binder and a Kovar lid are made of; "cobalt oxide" points at `metal.cobalt.oxide`, the calcined additive grade, and not at the ore, because the oxide a component maker buys is manufactured and the varistor's dopant is not a rock. "cobalt-nickel catalyst" points at the metal because a refinery's Co-Mo hydrotreating catalyst is made from the same refined cobalt as a cemented carbide. The last block was added by the phase 3 review of the ~30 highest-traffic unresolved input strings, and every one of the sixteen was read at every site it appears on rather than matched by name. Five notes on that block: (1) "sulphuric acid" and "sulfuric acid" are two spellings of one substance and both keys are needed, because normalisation strips punctuation but not the u; both point at the bulk 93-99% node, and the two sites that want electronic grade name `chem.fab-chemicals.sulfuric-acid` by id instead. (2) "steam" and "electricity" are cross-cutting utilities, so they attach as `from` edges like water and the gas supply already do; `facility.electricity` already had 173 such edges and `facility.steam` had none, so this is the first. (3) "abs melt" points at `chem.abs.grade`, the case grade; two nodes that carried the string while describing something else were corrected first - the case feet are rubber or soft PVC, and the shield spacer is greyboard or corrugated board. (4) "steel sheet" points at `metal.steel.sheet`, but the CRT shadow mask is photoetched from its own low-carbon sheet and now names that node by id. (5) "surfactant" points at the tape pigment's crystal-habit modifier, which is a fatty acid or alkylbenzene sulphonate; the deinking flotation cell on the packaging branch uses the same chemistry and now resolves there too, so if that node is ever moved the key has to move with it. No node exists for polystyrene as a substance, for polyphenylene sulfide, or for chrome alum, so those input strings are left unresolved rather than mapped to a near neighbour. Several entries still point at `process` nodes, which inverts the `from` relation: it reads as "this substance is made of this procedure". Fixing those properly needs material nodes for the substances, not a better mapping.
